title: Crisp Fried Mixed Seafood and Courgette with Lemon
summary: Prawns, squid, white fish and courgette batons in a featherlight sparkling-water batter, fried until crisp and finished with flaky salt, parsley and lemon. Best eaten the minute it comes out of the oil.
equipment: large heavy saucepan or Dutch oven (at least 5 litres)
deep-fry or probe thermometer that reads to 200 °C
2 wire racks set in rimmed baking trays

ingredients.item: raw peeled king prawns, tails left on, deveined
cleaned squid, tubes cut into 1.5 cm rings
skinless firm white fish fillet, cut into 2 cm strips
courgette, cut into 1 x 7 cm batons
fine sea salt or table salt
sunflower or vegetable oil, for deep-frying
fine sea salt or table salt
ingredients.note: about ¼ tsp; flaky sea salt, to finish

steps.title: Dry and chill
steps.text: Pat the prawns, squid, fish and courgette very dry with kitchen paper and keep them in the fridge. Set the oven to 100°C and line one rack with kitchen paper. Surface moisture makes oil spit and stops batter from clinging, so dry ingredients fry cleaner and crisper.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour the oil into the heavy pan, no more than one-third full, and heat it to 180°C. Check with the thermometer rather than guessing. Hot oil sets the batter instantly, sealing in moisture and keeping the coating from turning greasy.

steps.title: Whisk the batter
steps.text: Combine the flour, cornflour, baking powder and salt, then whisk in the ice-cold sparkling water just until smooth; a few small lumps are fine. Make it now, right before frying, while the bubbles are still lively. Cold water and minimal mixing limit gluten, and the bubbles expand in the oil to give a lacy, crisp crust.

steps.title: Dust and dip
steps.text: Toss a handful of courgette in the dusting flour and shake off the excess. Dip the pieces in the batter, letting the surplus drip back into the bowl. A dry flour layer gives the wet batter something to grip, so it does not slide off in the oil.

steps.title: Fry the courgette
steps.text: Lower the courgette into the oil one piece at a time so they do not stick together. Fry for 2-3 minutes, turning once, until pale golden and crisp, then move to the lined rack in the oven. Adding pieces individually keeps the oil temperature stable.

steps.title: Fry the seafood
steps.text: Work through the prawns, then the fish, then the squid in the same way, frying each batch for 2-3 minutes until golden. Inside, the seafood should be opaque, with the fish flaking and reaching at least 63°C. Let the oil return to 180°C and skim out loose bits between batches, so each one fries as crisply as the first.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Pile everything onto a warm platter, sprinkle with the flaky salt and parsley, and serve at once with lemon wedges. Salting straight away helps it stick to the hot, dry surface.

tips: A common mistake is making the batter too early: the bubbles go flat and the crust turns heavy, so whisk it just before you fry.
Keep the sparkling water in the fridge until the last moment, as cold batter gives a crisper result.
For safety, keep the pan handle turned in, never leave the oil unattended and keep a lid nearby; let the oil cool completely before moving it.
Do not cover the fried pieces while they wait, as trapped steam softens the coating.
storage: This is best eaten freshly fried. Cool any leftovers within 2 hours, refrigerate for up to 1 day and reheat on a rack in a hot oven until piping hot (74°C).
